neighbours.label: verb of passing someone's personal information on to others, as in privacy promises ('we will never share / sell / disclose your email'); not 'share' in other senses
fire: Enter your address below to get the weekly recipes. We will never share your details with other companies.
Subscribing is free, and the shop has promised that it does not sell its customers' addresses to marketers.
Our newsletter goes out once a month. We hate spam too and won't share your email with anybody.
The clinic keeps your records private and will not disclose your medical history to your employer.
Sign up for updates about the festival. Rest assured that we never give your phone number to third parties.
The app's policy states that the developers do not share users' locations with advertisers.
Your donation is confidential, and the charity will not pass your name on to other organisations.
Leave a comment below. Your email stays hidden and we will never sell it to anyone.
quiet: Enter your address below to get the weekly recipes. We send them out every Sunday morning before breakfast.
Subscribing is free, and the shop has promised that it will post a discount code every month.
Our newsletter goes out once a month. We hate long emails too and keep each one short.
The clinic keeps your records in a locked cabinet and will not open on public holidays.
The two sisters agreed to share the last slice of cake after dinner.
The app's policy states that the developers do not charge users for the basic version.
Your donation is tax deductible, and the charity will post a receipt to your home within a week.
He owns a large share in the bakery on the corner of our street.

notes: Probes: 'never share your email' 0.81, 'do not sell your personal data' 0.64, 'share a large pizza' 0.01, 'a large share of the market' 0.01; 'tell him the news' 0.32 and 'I'll pass it on' 0.48 suggest a wider passing-on-information sense.
